newsitem.title: GERMANY: East German ex-defence minister reports to jail.
newsitem.headline: East German ex-defence minister reports to jail.

text.p: Former East German defence minister Heinz Kessler and his ex-deputy Fritz Streletz reported to prison on Tuesday to begin sentences for the killing of East Germans trying to flee the country, Berlin's justice ministry said.

The Federal Constitutional Court two weeks ago confirmed sentences of 7-1/2 years for Kessler, 76, and 5-1/2 years for Streletz, 70, for manslaughter in connection with the Cold War killings along the Berlin Wall and the inner German border.

The court was hearing an appeal by Kessler, Streletz and Suhl regional communist party chief Hans Albrecht against a 1994 court verdict holding them responsible for the heavy fortifications and shoot-to-kill orders on the East German side of the border.
Spokeswoman Cornelia Bischoff said the men had had until Wednesday to report to Hakenfelde prison. She did not know why Kessler and Streletz had chosen to report a day early.
Albrecht faces a sentence of five years and one month.
Bischoff said they would be kept in a low-security part of the jail.
